townhall_clerk.text: Welcome to Manchester Town Hall. Mind the Gothic, it is everywhere.
Alfred Waterhouse designed it and it opened in 1877. He later did the Natural History Museum in London.
The clock tower is about 85 metres tall, and the biggest bell is called Great Abel.
It is named after Abel Heywood, a former mayor. Mayors do like their names on things.

then.text: The Definitive Map and Statement is the legal record. If it isn't on the map, it isn't a path, however many boots have worn it. The Act of 1949 made councils keep one.
Yours is on, as of this morning. I stamped it myself.
A tin box and a minute book. Well, well. Evidence of use, going back to before the war. That's what the Highways Act asks: twenty years of use, as of right, without being stopped.
I'll lodge it as a modification order claim for the High Moor path. It will take a while. It always takes a while. But I can see no honest objection.

else.text: Minutes are good. Is there anything else? Photographs, letters, anything saying people walked it before the war.
I'd need proof that people walked it. Minutes, diaries, photographs. Ezra Hollins in Goyt Valley says there are some somewhere.
A path claim? That's a long form. Come back when you've evidence of walking. Twenty years, as of right, without being stopped.
